name: Question 2
problem:
Let $A$ be a $2\times 2$ matrix with eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=-1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=2$ corresponding to the eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ respectively, where

$$
{v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Solve the following initial value problem:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),
$$

where $A$ has two distinct eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2},$ the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the general solution to our matrix differential equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}$, we substitute $t=0$ in the general solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(0) & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{-0}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2(0)} & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2} \\ 5{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{c}_{1}+2{c}_{2}=4 \\ 5{c}_{1}-2{c}_{2}=8.\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we get

$$
6{c}_{1}=12\,⟹\,{c}_{1}=2.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
2+2{c}_{2}=4\,⟹\,{c}_{2}=1.
$$

 

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+1[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 10\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t}+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2\end{aligned}]{e}^{2t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let A be a 2×2 matrix with eigenvalues λ1=−1 and λ2=2 corresponding to the eigenvectors v1 and v2 respectively, where v1=[15],v2=[2−2]. Solve the following initial value problem: x′(t)=Ax(t),x(0)=[48]

a
x(t)=[15]e−t+[33]e2t
b
x(t)=[−1−5]e−t+[513]e2t
c
x(t)=[18]e−t+[30]e2t
d
x(t)=[66]e−t+[−22]e2t
e
x(t)=[210]e−t+[2−2]e2t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form x′(t)=Ax(t), where A has two distinct eigenvalues λ1,λ2 with corresponding eigenvectors v1 and v2, the formula for the general solution is x(t)=c1v1eλ1t+c2v2eλ2t,c1,c2∈R.

Therefore, the general solution to our matrix differential equation is x(t)=c1[15]e−t+c2[2−2]e2t,c1,c2∈R.

Now, to find the values of c1 and c2, we substitute t=0 in the general solution:

x(0)=[48]c1[15]e−0+c2[2−2]e2(0)=[48][c1+2c25c1−2c2]=[48]

So, we have a system of linear equations {c1+2c2=45c1−2c2=8. Adding the equations, we get 6c1=12⟹c1=2. Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 2+2c2=4⟹c2=1.

Therefore, the solution to the initial value problem is x(t)=2[15]e−t+1[2−2]e2t=[210]e−t+[2−2]e2t.
